about: The card-only recipes of the image and edit routes: which (route, family, quant) may run across two cards, which loader puts which weight on which card, and the per-card VRAM peak a call is held to. cuda:0 is the STORAGE card (text encoder, VAE, the donor blocks of the DiT), cuda:1 the COMPUTE card (the DiT's resident share and the sampler's activations); render/multicard-recipes.mjs reads this file and internal/hostneed keeps a copy of the figures (a Go test pins the two). maxPixels, when present, is the largest canvas (width times height, in pixels) a call on the row may ask for, and maxPixelsNote says where the number comes from; the runner refuses a larger canvas by name (canvasRefusal), where maxMegapixels is the edit canvas the compute peak was scaled to (the edit runner refuses a pinned canvas above it). blocked, when present, is a sentence: the row exists but the runner refuses it by name until the thing it says was run is run (a held-back row is no recipe to the estimate, the doctor and the typed doors; its data stays for the proof arm). basis is 'measured' only for a row whose per-card peak was read in a run that used the read-only safetensors loader (a card-only run that charged no weights to host commit); every image arm of the 2026-10-11 two-card benchmark ran the stock loader, so those rows are 'predicted' and a call on them declares the ordinary estimate until a live run with the read-only loader promotes them.

rows.maxPixelsNote: measured at 2048x2048 (4,194,304 pixels, the qwen-image-2.1 family default), the cap; no larger canvas has been run card-only
rows.evidence: Measured 2026-10-20 on the 5070 Ti (compute) and a 5060 Ti (storage), launched compute-first (cuda:0 is the compute card), with the live fast binding's file (qwen-image-2.1-UC-int8_convrot, 6.76 GiB). The bf16 Qwen3-VL-8B text encoder (16.33 GiB) is built off the cards by the harness's OffloadCLIPLoaderDisTorch2 and placed by cuda:1,5gb;cuda:0,* in 6.1 s: cuda:0 11.36 GiB, cuda:1 4.97 GiB, 0 GiB on the CPU; OffloadFreeAfterEncode then frees both cards in 0.8 s (14.51 and 14.80 GiB free) before the int8 DiT loads whole on cuda:0, where comfy_kitchen's int8 kernels run. 2048x2048, 40 steps at 2.57 s/it: 179.9 s. Per-card peaks by phase: the encoder 12.27 GiB on the compute card and 5.09 on the storage card, the sampler 9.04 GiB on the compute card (the 6.76 GiB DiT and 2.3 GiB of activations and context), the VAE decode 5.84 GiB on the storage card. Host physical memory dipped to 50.6 GiB free (from 84.5) for about 10 s while the encoder was staged on its way to the cards and held at 81.7 through sampling; no weight stayed in host RAM. The 2026-10-11 benchmark had run the same DiT across two cards in 213.4 s with the display card as one of them, pixel-identical to the single-card render.

rows.maxPixelsNote: measured at 2048x2048 (4,194,304 pixels, the qwen-image-2.1 family default), the cap; no larger canvas has been run card-only
rows.evidence: Measured 2026-10-20 on the 5070 Ti (compute) and a 5060 Ti (storage), launched compute-first (cuda:0 is the compute card) because the 2.1 model's comfy_kitchen fused kernels run on cuda:0 only: the storage-first launch aborted at the first sampler step after ComfyUI-MultiGPU CPU-staged tensors from cuda:1 to cuda:0 (upstream issue 220). The bf16 Qwen3-VL-8B text encoder (16.33 GiB, more than a card) is built off the cards by the harness's OffloadCLIPLoaderDisTorch2 (a stock CLIPLoaderDisTorch2MultiGPU ran out of memory 1.4 s in, because under --gpu-only ComfyUI builds the whole encoder on one card before the split applies) and placed by cuda:1,8gb;cuda:0,* in 7.3 s: cuda:0 8.33 GiB, cuda:1 8.00 GiB, 0 GiB on the CPU. OffloadFreeAfterEncode then frees both cards in 0.8 s (cuda:0 back to 14.48 GiB free, cuda:1 to 14.80) before the DiT, built empty and filled from the read-only map, lands 8 GiB on cuda:0 and 5.25 GiB on cuda:1. 2048x2048, 40 steps at 5.57 s/it: 280.0 s, peaks 10.90 GiB on the compute card and 8.12 GiB on the storage card. Host physical memory dipped only while the weights streamed to the cards (64.6 GiB free at the encoder load and 75.0 at the DiT load, from 83.9) and held at 81 GiB through sampling; no weight stayed in host RAM. The 2026-10-11 benchmark had run the same bf16 DiT all-VRAM across two cards in 357.5 s, pixel-identical to the single-card render, with the display card as the donor.

rows.maxPixelsNote: measured at 1328x1328 (1,763,584 pixels, the family default) and 928x1664: the cap is 1536x1152 (1,769,472), 0.3 % above the larger measured canvas
rows.evidence: 2512 bf16 (38 GiB) fits no card, so 2512 is the Q5_1 GGUF (14.3 GiB). Measured 2026-10-20 on the 5070 Ti (compute, cuda:1) and a 5060 Ti (storage, cuda:0), 10 GiB of the DiT resident on the compute card, the fp8 text encoder whole on the storage card and freed after the encode, full preset (50 steps, cfg 4): 1328x1328 in 415.2 s with peaks 11.84 GiB on the compute card and 8.26 GiB on the storage card; 928x1664 in 401.3 s with peaks 11.74 and 8.26 GiB. Host physical memory stayed within 3.5 GiB of where it started for the whole run, beyond a dip while the weights streamed to the cards. Commit grew by about the VRAM in use, which Windows charges to commit under WDDM; no weight was charged. The storage peak is the text-encode stage (encoder, VAE, context); the compute peak is the resident share plus the sampler's activations. The earlier 3 GiB resident share ran out of memory on the storage card at 928x1664, which is why 10 GiB of the DiT sits on the compute card.

rows.maxPixelsNote: measured at 1536x1024 (1,572,864 pixels): the default 1024x1024 is inside it, the 2048x1024 bake-off canvas is not
rows.evidence: The bf16 DiT (24.48 GiB) with the Qwen3-VL-4B bf16 text encoder (8.27 GiB) is 33 GiB of weights, more than one card and less than the pair. Measured 2026-10-20 on the 5070 Ti (compute, cuda:1) and a 5060 Ti (storage, cuda:0), turbo recipe (8 steps, cfg 1): 1536x1024 with 11 GiB of the DiT resident on the compute card in 68.5 s, peaks 13.15 GiB on the compute card and 13.10 GiB on the storage card; 1024x1024 with 12 GiB resident in 82.1 s, peaks 14.30 and 12.10 GiB. The text encoder is built whole on the storage card for the encode and freed before the DiT's blocks land (--cache-none). Host physical memory came back to within 2.5 GiB of where it started, beyond a dip while the weights streamed to the cards; no weight was charged to host commit. The run needs the harness pack's lazy diffusion-model build (render/comfyui-ext): stock ComfyUI builds an unquantized DiT whole on the storage card before DisTorch2 splits it, and the first card-only run of this row ran out of memory there, 23 s in, with 15.03 GiB allocated.

Benchmark 2026-10-11, section 4.6: fp8mixed (19.1 GiB) at 1.47 MP on two 5060 Ti with the read-only loader, compute card 9 GiB resident, 10.1 GiB on the storage card, bypass LoRA: success in 145.5 s (9.4 s per step), peaks 11.9 GiB on the compute card and 10.9 GiB on the storage card, host growth 1.87 GiB. The figures here are the compute peak scaled to the 2.0 MP cap of the edit canvas (activations 2.6 GiB at 1.47 MP, 3.5 at 2.0) and the storage peak rounded up. One card cannot hold the model (OOM at the load), the merging LoRA loader ran out of memory, so the bypass loader is part of the recipe.

Benchmark 2026-10-11, section 4.6: Q5_1 GGUF at 1.47 MP on two 5060 Ti with every weight on the storage card: success in 192.3 s but only 0.3 GiB free there, 'too thin for production'; the benchmark's own prediction for a 3 GiB resident share on the compute card is storage about 12.6 GiB and compute about 4.9 GiB at that 1.47 MP canvas, not run. The compute figure here is scaled to the 2.0 MP cap this row claims, as the fp8mixed row's is: the 1.9 GiB the compute card held at 1.4727 MP grows to 2.6 GiB, so 3 + 2.6 = 5.6 GiB. The run used the read-only loader (host growth 1.50 GiB).
